system:
You are an art-world editor compiling a gallery guide for Tokyo, Japan. Answer with the
JSON object the schema describes and nothing else. Rank by significance and influence in the
contemporary art world: programme quality, the artists represented, art-fair presence, critical and
institutional attention, and longevity. Include commercial galleries and the nonprofit, artist-run and
project spaces that show contemporary art to the public in Tokyo itself (galleries whose home is
elsewhere count only through a permanent Tokyo space). Exclude museums, art fairs, auction houses,
framers, art schools, decor shops, online-only dealers and advisories. For every gallery give its usual
name; its official website when you are confident of it, else null; the district it is in, using one of
these labels when it fits (Roppongi, Ginza/Kyobashi, Nihonbashi/Bakurocho, Shibuya/Omotesando, Shinjuku/Kagurazaka, Ebisu/Meguro, Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tennozu, Ueno/Yanaka, Setagaya/West Tokyo) else the district name you know; a street address hint when you
know it (street and number are enough), else null; its kind (gallery, museum, nonprofit, project_space, university, other); and a short note on why it
matters. Every entry must be a distinct venue — list a gallery with several Tokyo spaces once.
user: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Tokyo, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: SCAI THE BATHHOUSE
galleries.note: Landmark bathhouse gallery with exceptional postwar and contemporary Japanese artists, international fairs and deep institutional reach.

galleries.name: Taka Ishii Gallery
galleries.note: Central to Japanese contemporary art since the 1990s, with a formidable roster spanning conceptual art, painting and photography.

galleries.name: Ota Fine Arts
galleries.note: Internationally influential gallery closely associated with Yayoi Kusama and major artists from Japan and Southeast Asia.

galleries.name: Tomio Koyama Gallery
galleries.note: Pivotal in establishing the global reputations of Yoshitomo Nara, Takashi Murakami and a generation of Japanese painters.

galleries.name: ShugoArts
galleries.note: Museum-caliber programme led by major Japanese artists including Masato Kobayashi, Shigeo Toya and Yukio Fujimoto.

galleries.name: Mizuma Art Gallery
galleries.note: Long-running international gallery known for politically and socially engaged art from Japan and across Asia.

galleries.name: Perrotin Tokyo
galleries.note: Tokyo branch of the influential global gallery, presenting internationally prominent artists alongside Japanese figures.

galleries.name: Pace Gallery Tokyo
galleries.note: Major global gallery whose substantial Azabudai space brings blue-chip contemporary and postwar programmes to Tokyo.

galleries.name: Hauser & Wirth Tokyo
galleries.note: Permanent Tokyo outpost of one of the world's most powerful galleries, with exhibitions by internationally canonical artists.

galleries.name: NANZUKA UNDERGROUND
galleries.note: Globally visible platform connecting contemporary art with underground culture, illustration, design and popular media.

galleries.name: Kaikai Kiki Gallery
galleries.note: Takashi Murakami's influential gallery platform for Japanese and international artists linked to contemporary visual culture.

galleries.name: Take Ninagawa
galleries.note: Critically respected programme of conceptually rigorous artists, with strong biennial, institutional and international-fair visibility.

galleries.name: Wako Works of Art
galleries.note: A leading Tokyo gallery for European and Japanese conceptual practices, distinguished by longevity and scholarly exhibitions.

galleries.name: Misako & Rosen
galleries.note: Internationally connected gallery whose adventurous programme has introduced important Japanese and overseas artists.

galleries.name: Gallery Koyanagi
galleries.note: Prestigious Ginza gallery representing major conceptual and photographic artists, including Hiroshi Sugimoto and Sophie Calle.

galleries.name: ANOMALY
galleries.note: Ambitious large-scale gallery formed from three respected predecessors, with an established roster of leading Japanese artists.

galleries.name: Yutaka Kikutake Gallery
galleries.note: Highly regarded younger gallery supporting rigorous emerging and mid-career artists with growing institutional recognition.

galleries.name: KOSAKU KANECHIKA
galleries.note: Fast-rising gallery with a strong generation of Japanese artists and regular participation in major international fairs.

galleries.name: KOTARO NUKAGA
galleries.note: Expanding contemporary programme pairing prominent international names with established and emerging Japanese artists.

galleries.name: BLUM Tokyo
galleries.note: Tokyo branch of the influential Los Angeles gallery long involved in exchanges between Japanese and American contemporary art.

galleries.name: TARO NASU
galleries.note: A key gallery for conceptual, minimalist and post-conceptual art, with a distinguished roster and sustained critical standing.

galleries.name: MUJIN-TO Production
galleries.note: Artist-focused gallery noted for experimental Japanese practices and strong relationships with curators and public institutions.

galleries.name: Gallery SIDE 2
galleries.note: Independent gallery with a long record of presenting critically ambitious Japanese and international contemporary artists.

galleries.name: MAHO KUBOTA GALLERY
galleries.note: Internationally oriented gallery recognized for carefully developed exhibitions by emerging and established artists.

galleries.name: MAKI Gallery
galleries.note: Prominent multi-space gallery with an increasingly international roster and substantial presence at Asian and global fairs.

galleries.name: Tokyo Gallery + BTAP
galleries.note: Founded in 1950, this historically crucial gallery fostered Japanese avant-garde art and early exchange with China and Korea.

galleries.name: Shiseido Gallery
galleries.note: One of Japan's oldest active art spaces, supporting experimental contemporary exhibitions through a major cultural programme.

galleries.name: THE CLUB
galleries.note: Curatorially driven Ginza gallery presenting historically important postwar and contemporary artists in an international context.

galleries.name: Whitestone Gallery
galleries.note: Large, long-established dealer with particular strength in Gutai, postwar Japanese art and an expanding Asian network.

galleries.name: Fergus McCaffrey Tokyo
galleries.note: Scholarly international gallery especially important for postwar Japanese avant-gardes and cross-Pacific art histories.

galleries.name: Gallery MoMo
galleries.note: Established contemporary gallery with a consistent Japanese and international programme and long-standing fair participation.

galleries.name: Aoyama Meguro
galleries.note: Small but critically influential gallery associated with conceptually precise artists and Tokyo's independent scene.

galleries.name: Tokyo Opera City Art Gallery
galleries.note: Major non-collecting exhibition venue presenting substantial surveys, commissions and thematic contemporary-art exhibitions.

galleries.name: Tokyo Arts and Space
galleries.note: Tokyo Metropolitan Government platform supporting experimental exhibitions, residencies and emerging artists with international exchange.

galleries.name: XYZcollective
galleries.note: Internationally recognized artist-run initiative whose collaborative programme has helped reshape Tokyo's younger gallery ecology.

galleries.name: KAYOKOYUKI
galleries.note: Critically respected gallery representing an influential group of younger Japanese conceptual and multimedia artists.

galleries.name: WAITINGROOM
galleries.note: Independent gallery with a strong record of nurturing emerging artists and placing their work in institutional exhibitions.

galleries.name: gallery αM
galleries.note: Curator-led public gallery supported by Musashino Art University, known for experimental series and early-career commissions.

galleries.name: Satoko Oe Contemporary
galleries.note: Focused programme of intellectually rigorous Japanese artists, many with growing museum and biennial attention.

galleries.name: HAGIWARA PROJECTS
galleries.note: Respected project-based gallery supporting emerging and mid-career artists through closely curated exhibitions.

galleries.name: PARCEL
galleries.note: Distinctive contemporary space in a former parking structure, with a cross-disciplinary and internationally connected programme.

galleries.name: GALLERY COMMON
galleries.note: Visible platform for younger contemporary art at the intersection of painting, street culture and design.

galleries.name: EUKARYOTE
galleries.note: Emerging-artist gallery noted for polished exhibitions across painting, sculpture, installation and new media.

galleries.name: TAV GALLERY
galleries.note: Independent gallery closely associated with experimental, internet-aware and politically alert younger Japanese practices.

galleries.name: KEN NAKAHASHI
galleries.note: Critically minded gallery presenting distinctive emerging and established artists in an intimate Shinjuku setting.

galleries.name: Yumiko Chiba Associates
galleries.note: Research-oriented gallery especially important for reassessing Japanese conceptual, photographic and postwar practices.

galleries.name: √K Contemporary
galleries.note: Spacious Kagurazaka-area gallery mounting ambitious exhibitions of modern, postwar and contemporary Japanese art.

galleries.name: Maki Fine Arts
galleries.note: Long-running independent gallery known for thoughtful presentations of Japanese painters, sculptors and conceptual artists.

galleries.name: eitoeiko
galleries.note: Independent gallery with an eclectic, socially attentive programme spanning emerging practices and historical rediscoveries.

galleries.name: KOKI ARTS
galleries.note: Well-regarded gallery supporting emerging Japanese and international artists through concise, carefully installed exhibitions.

galleries.name: HARMAS GALLERY
galleries.note: Independent space recognized for understated, critically rigorous exhibitions by younger Japanese artists.

galleries.name: Sprout Curation
galleries.note: Curatorially focused gallery pairing contemporary practice with research into postwar Japanese art and visual culture.

galleries.name: KANA KAWANISHI GALLERY
galleries.note: Strong contemporary and photographic programme emphasizing conceptually engaged artists and international dialogue.

galleries.name: CON_
galleries.note: Young gallery gaining attention for experimental exhibitions and close engagement with Tokyo's emerging artist community.
Artist-run space with an outsized international reputation for collaborative, irreverent and generation-defining exhibitions.

galleries.name: SNOW Contemporary
galleries.note: Established gallery presenting socially engaged installation, performance, media art and contemporary Japanese visual culture.

galleries.name: CLEAR GALLERY TOKYO
galleries.note: Internationally oriented gallery with a programme spanning contemporary art, design and historically informed presentations.

galleries.name: hiromiyoshii
galleries.note: Veteran contemporary dealer and project platform with longstanding connections across Japan's international art scene.

galleries.name: Gallery ETHER
galleries.note: Emerging gallery presenting multicultural and interdisciplinary practices, often by artists working between Japan and abroad.

galleries.name: Gallery 38
galleries.note: Focused gallery building dialogue between Japanese and Chinese contemporary artists through restrained, research-led exhibitions.

galleries.name: PGI
galleries.note: One of Tokyo's most important photography galleries, with major Japanese estates and a strong international programme.

galleries.name: Zen Foto Gallery
galleries.note: Internationally influential specialist in Asian photography, supported by an active and respected publishing programme.

galleries.name: Akio Nagasawa Gallery
galleries.note: Leading photography gallery and publisher associated with important Japanese photographers and meticulously produced editions.

galleries.name: MEM
galleries.note: Historically informed gallery with particular strength in Japanese photography, performance documentation and experimental postwar art.

galleries.name: G/P gallery
galleries.note: Influential platform for contemporary photography that has supported new Japanese image-makers, publications and curatorial projects.

galleries.name: Art Front Gallery
galleries.note: Long-established Daikanyama gallery linked to major public-art commissions, regional art projects and Japanese contemporary artists.

galleries.name: POETIC SCAPE
galleries.note: Respected specialist gallery for contemporary photography, known for sustained artist development and thoughtful exhibitions.

galleries.name: The 5th Floor
galleries.note: Independent curatorial space in a former ryotei, hosting experimental exhibitions, research and international collaborations.

galleries.name: Art Center Ongoing
galleries.note: Essential artist-led centre for emerging practices, performances, talks and community-building in western Tokyo.

galleries.name: Youkobo Art Space
galleries.note: Long-running residency and exhibition space fostering sustained exchange between Tokyo artists and international visitors.

galleries.name: Spiral Garden
galleries.note: Prominent public exhibition space where contemporary art, design, craft and performance reach a broad Tokyo audience.

galleries.name: GYRE GALLERY
galleries.note: Architecturally ambitious Omotesando venue presenting curator-led exhibitions on art, ecology, architecture and social change.

galleries.name: Espace Louis Vuitton Tokyo
galleries.note: Foundation-run exhibition space bringing major international artists and collection projects to a prominent Omotesando location.

galleries.name: Le Forum, Ginza Maison Hermès
galleries.note: Architecturally notable foundation space with a sustained record of commissioned and curatorially ambitious contemporary exhibitions.

galleries.name: CHANEL NEXUS HALL
galleries.note: Corporate cultural venue best known for polished photography and contemporary-art exhibitions with international reach.

galleries.name: THE MASS
galleries.note: Independent Harajuku complex mounting high-profile exhibitions across contemporary art, photography, fashion and design.

galleries.name: CALM & PUNK GALLERY
galleries.note: Cross-disciplinary gallery connecting contemporary art with influential graphic-design, music and fashion communities.

galleries.name: GALLERY TARGET
galleries.note: Established Harajuku gallery influential in street-derived, illustrative and pop-oriented contemporary art.

galleries.name: SAI
galleries.note: Highly visible Miyashita Park gallery presenting contemporary artists connected to painting, music, fashion and youth culture.

galleries.name: GALLERY X BY PARCO
galleries.note: Prominent cultural-retail gallery hosting contemporary art, photography, publishing and popular-culture collaborations.

galleries.name: OIL by Bijutsu Techo Gallery
galleries.note: Physical exhibition arm of a major Japanese art-media platform, providing visibility and sales support to contemporary artists.

galleries.name: NADiff Gallery
galleries.note: Exhibition space within Tokyo's key specialist art bookstore, important for artist publications and experimental projects.

galleries.name: LOKO GALLERY
galleries.note: Independent multi-level gallery presenting emerging and mid-career artists in painting, installation and interdisciplinary media.

galleries.name: CAGE GALLERY
galleries.note: Street-facing, always-visible project space whose compact installations extend contemporary art into everyday urban space.

galleries.name: Tokyo International Gallery
galleries.note: Tennozu gallery with a globally oriented emerging programme and growing participation in Asian art fairs.

galleries.name: Contemporary Tokyo
galleries.note: Cross-border gallery connecting Japanese contemporary artists with collectors and institutions across Greater China and Asia.

galleries.name: Takuro Someya Contemporary Art
galleries.note: Established gallery, also known as TSCA, supporting conceptually focused Japanese artists and international exchange.

galleries.name: YOD Gallery Tokyo
galleries.note: Permanent Tokyo branch of the Osaka gallery, presenting contemporary Japanese art with particular attention to material traditions.

galleries.name: A Lighthouse called Kanata
galleries.note: Internationally active gallery advancing sculptural and craft-rooted Japanese artists through major fairs and institutional placements.

galleries.name: taguchi fine art
galleries.note: Independent gallery with a durable programme of Japanese and European artists and a strong emphasis on painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: GALLERY HASHIMOTO
galleries.note: Established contemporary gallery recognized for carefully sustained relationships with Japanese painters and sculptors.

galleries.name: CASHI
galleries.note: Independent gallery with an experimental programme spanning emerging art, performance, installation and collaborative projects.

galleries.name: Galerie Tokyo Humanité
galleries.note: Long-running gallery respected for serious presentations of Japanese painting, sculpture, printmaking and installation.

galleries.name: Gallery Tsubaki
galleries.note: Veteran Kyobashi gallery with decades of commitment to idiosyncratic Japanese contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Yamaki Fine Art
galleries.note: Established gallery presenting Japanese postwar and contemporary work with a research-conscious, historically grounded approach.

galleries.name: Galerie Nichido
galleries.note: One of Japan's longest-established commercial galleries, influential in modern yōga and continuing contemporary painting programmes.

galleries.name: Toki-no-Wasuremono
galleries.note: Scholarly gallery and publisher connecting contemporary work with modern architecture, prints, photography and Japanese avant-gardes.

galleries.name: Gallery Naruyama
galleries.note: Singular gallery known for uncompromising figurative, photographic and subcultural positions outside Tokyo's mainstream market.

galleries.name: 104GALERIE
galleries.note: Nakameguro gallery with a sustained international programme emphasizing materially expressive painting and sculpture.

galleries.name: photographers' gallery
galleries.note: Influential photographer-run space supporting independent exhibitions, criticism and publishing outside the conventional commercial system.
